title: Named Plate Boundaries
_note: Hand-maintained (not derived from the seed CSV). `pairs` and `bbox` drive scripts/generate_named_boundary_maps.py: pairs are PB2002 plate codes (order-insensitive), bbox is [lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max] and selects which segments of that plate pair belong to this named boundary. A bbox whose lon_min > lon_max wraps the antimeridian.

concepts.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
concepts.definition: The spreading centre running the length of the Atlantic, where new ocean floor is created along a rift valley at the ridge crest; it breaches sea level in Iceland and the Azores.

concepts.name: East Pacific Rise
concepts.definition: The fastest-spreading ridge on Earth, opening the eastern Pacific at up to about 150 mm a year and lined with hydrothermal vents.

concepts.name: East African Rift
concepts.definition: A continental rift splitting the African Plate into the Nubian and Somali plates, the clearest place on land to watch a divergent boundary tear a continent apart.

concepts.name: Red Sea Rift
concepts.definition: The spreading centre pulling Arabia away from Africa, an incipient ocean basin that has already flooded to become the Red Sea.

concepts.name: San Andreas Fault
concepts.definition: A right-lateral strike-slip fault running about 1,200 km through California, where the Pacific Plate slides north-west past North America.

concepts.name: Alpine Fault
concepts.definition: The boundary running the length of New Zealand's South Island, right-lateral but with a strong reverse component, so it both offsets and lifts.

concepts.name: Dead Sea Transform
concepts.alt_names: Dead Sea Rift, Jordan Rift Valley
concepts.definition: A left-lateral transform running from the Gulf of Aqaba to southern Turkey, along which Arabia slides north past Africa.

concepts.name: North Scotia Ridge
concepts.definition: The left-lateral transform forming the northern edge of the Scotia Sea, where the small Scotia Plate slides past South America at about 7 mm a year.

concepts.name: Himalayan collision zone
concepts.definition: The continent-to-continent collision where India drives into Asia; with no dense ocean plate to sink, the crust thickens and rises instead of subducting.

concepts.name: Zagros fold belt
concepts.definition: The collision zone where Arabia pushes into Eurasia, crumpling the sedimentary cover of Iran into long parallel folds.

concepts.name: Peru–Chile Trench
concepts.definition: The trench running the length of South America's Pacific margin, where the Nazca Plate dives under the continent.

concepts.name: Sunda Trench
concepts.definition: The subduction zone off Sumatra and Java; its 2004 megathrust rupture caused the Indian Ocean tsunami.

concepts.name: Mariana Trench
concepts.definition: The deepest trench on Earth, reaching about 10,900 m at Challenger Deep, where old cold Pacific floor sinks almost vertically.

concepts.name: Middle America Trench
concepts.definition: The subduction zone off western Mexico and Central America that feeds the volcanic chain from Popocatépetl to Costa Rica.

concepts.name: Cascadia subduction zone
concepts.definition: A quiet-looking offshore megathrust from northern California to Vancouver Island that locks for centuries between magnitude-9 ruptures.

concepts.name: Aleutian Trench
concepts.definition: The 3,400 km trench arcing from Kamchatka to the Gulf of Alaska, where the Pacific Plate sinks at about 7.5 cm a year.

concepts.name: Lesser Antilles arc
concepts.definition: The curved chain of volcanic islands from Saba to Grenada, built where Atlantic floor of the South American Plate subducts beneath the Caribbean.
